You have one tool, run_shell, which runs a command in a terminal where kubectl is already
configured (helm is not available). Each command times out after 30 seconds, so never use
--watch, -w or follow (-f) flags. You can run at most 30 commands for this task;
after that you will be asked for your conclusion.
This is a diagnosis-only task: investigate the reported problem and find its root cause,
but do not change anything in the cluster.
When you are finished, reply without calling any tool. End your reply with one JSON object on its
own line: {"incident": true or false, "component": "<kind>/<name> of the root cause, or null",
"summary": "<one or two sentences>"}. Name the component as the Kubernetes object at fault (for
example deployment/payment, service/cart, node/<node name>); for one of the shop's feature flags,

Every order fails at checkout since this morning's checkout releases. Find the cause and fix it.

Release 3.1.1 moved checkout's PAYMENT_ADDR out of the Deployment into the ConfigMap `checkout-settings` (envFrom), still with the right value payment:8080. Afterwards the ConfigMap was edited in place to payment:8081, and release 3.1.2 (only a version bump) restarted checkout, which picked up the wrong address: every order fails at the payment step. A ConfigMap is not part of a Deployment revision, so `kubectl rollout undo` goes back to 3.1.1, which reads the same edited ConfigMap and stays broken. The ConfigMap value has to be fixed, and checkout restarted because environment variables are read only at start.
